proposedGenericDecision: This is a multi-country roster of named foreign NRENs (DFN, SWITCH, JANET/Jisc) each enumerated with their branded sub-services (X-WiN, DFN-CERT, SWITCHaai, SWITCHdrive, SWITCHengines, SWITCH-CERT). It illustrates the "common NREN architectural pattern" and supports the federation-precedent argument, but it hard-binds a specific set of national NRENs and their commercial service brands. Generalise to "peer NRENs in comparable jurisdictions, each operating a national backbone, a CSIRT, and federated identity/storage/IaaS services"; retain at most a jurisdiction-neutral exemplar subset under the evidence-methodology named-precedent allowance, and parameterize the branded service trio so it is not presented as the reference design. ANCHOR-NREN/ANCHOR-NREN-CSIRT cover the home NREN (RESTENA) only; ANCHOR-NREN mentions "DFN in Germany and SWITCH in Switzerland" in a single passing surfaceForm but does not treat this enumerated peer-NREN roster or its branded sub-services as a parameterizable unit.
rationale: Transversal scan shows DFN/X-WiN/DFN-CERT, SWITCHaai/SWITCHdrive/SWITCHengines/SWITCH-CERT, and JANET/Jisc recur across the dedicated NREN section, the institutional-examples section, and the CSIRT enumeration, yet a full-matrix scan returns 0 for X-WiN, SWITCHaai, SWITCHengines, DFN-CERT, Jisc, Janet and GARR. The matrix only incidentally lists DFN/SWITCH inside ANCHOR-NREN prose; the branded peer-NREN service roster is a genuinely uncovered national-infrastructure binding.

proposedGenericDecision: This service catalogue names specific GÉANT/region-operated service brands (eduroam, GÉANT TCS, perfSONAR-as-service, Globus, FER) and binds each to a specific operator (GÉANT, ESnet, RENATER, U. Chicago). These are distinct from the eduGAIN interfederation profile (ANCHOR-IDENTITY-FEDERATION) and from the GÉANT-backbone precedent (ANCHOR-GEANT-BACKBONE). Generalise to "the NREN-provided federated-service catalogue (federated Wi-Fi, trusted certificate service, performance monitoring, managed research-data transfer)" and parameterize the operator brands per region; keep eduroam/Globus/perfSONAR only as jurisdiction-neutral exemplar tools where the architecture genuinely depends on them. The FER French identity federation is RENATER-jurisdiction-bound and should be parameterized to "the national identity federation".
rationale: GÉANT TCS, the Trusted Certificate Service, and Globus return 0 on a full-matrix scan; eduroam and perfSONAR appear in the matrix only as incidental tokens inside ANCHOR-IDENTITY-FEDERATION / ANCHOR-NREN / ANCHOR-GEANT-BACKBONE prose, never as a parameterizable NREN service catalogue. The FER token in the matrix is a substring match (transfer/reference), not the French federation. The branded operator-to-service binding table is a genuinely uncovered national-infrastructure specificity.

location: ul-it-policy/book-public/public-body-sec07-nren.tex (GÉANT/RENATER capacity L18-24; campus connection L73-74); ul-it-policy/main/main-body-EN.tex (GÉANT scale L2655-2657, RENATER multi-100 Gbps L2660ish, SWITCH 100+ Gbps L2179, bandwidth row L1614); ul-it-policy/main/glossary-defs.tex (\glsdefine{geant}, L89); ul-it-policy/main/glossary-EN.tex (GÉANT 50 million users / 10,000+ institutions L241); ul-it-policy/book-public/public-body-sec03-specificities.tex (bandwidth 10--400 Gbps L59)
proposedGenericDecision: These are region-bound quantitative claims about the European backbone (40+ NRENs, 50 million users, 10,000+ institutions, 400 Gbps wavelengths, multi-100 Gbps national backbones). They are tied to the EU/GÉANT footprint and would be wrong for a non-European deployment. Keep the campus-connection capacity range (10--100 Gbps) as a jurisdiction-neutral engineering figure, but parameterize or generalise the GÉANT-specific membership and backbone-capacity numbers to "the regional research backbone (membership and backbone capacity per region)". Treat as sourced statistics under the abstract-over-quantitative-self-references convention: keep with citation when the EU edition is in scope, parameterize for the jurisdiction-agnostic edition.
rationale: "400 Gbps", "national backbone", "wavelength" and the GÉANT membership figures return 0 on a full-matrix scan, and no amount/cost anchor (ANCHOR-SANCTION-CEILING, ANCHOR-IT-SPEND-BENCHMARK, ANCHOR-FTE-ENVELOPE) covers backbone-capacity or NREN-membership quantities. These EU/GÉANT-footprint figures are an uncovered region-bound national-infrastructure quantitative binding.

surfaceForm: National/NREN research cloud as the down-scaled compute-sourcing option, with region-bound exemplars: "compute and storage are drawn from a national research cloud, an NREN service, or a managed provider under a data-processing agreement"; "existing research cloud infrastructure provided by NRENs (SWITCHengines, EGI Federated Cloud, GÉANT services)"; "AARNet (Australia), EGI Federated Cloud (Europe), SWITCHengines (Switzerland)".
location: ul-it-policy/argumentation/argumentation-body-EN.tex (down-scaled sourcing profile, L789); ul-it-policy/main/main-body-EN.tex (research-cloud sourcing options L3696-3700); ul-it-policy/technical/ch26-wave8-workload-EN.tex (EGI federated cloud L246); ul-it-policy/technical/ch27-wave9-lifecycle-EN.tex (EGI federations L241); ul-it-policy/technical/ch23-wave5-pilot-EN.tex (EGI / EUDAT L260)
proposedGenericDecision: The "national research cloud / NREN-provided cloud" sourcing option is a structurally generic argument, but it is instantiated with region-bound branded exemplars (SWITCHengines = Switzerland, EGI Federated Cloud = Europe, AARNet = Australia, GÉANT services) that presuppose a research-cloud ecosystem available in the deployer's jurisdiction. Generalise to "a national/regional research cloud or NREN-provided cloud service, where one exists" and parameterize the named cloud exemplars per region; flag that for jurisdictions without an NREN research cloud the managed-provider fallback is the only path. Distinct from ANCHOR-EUROHPC-SYSTEM (the EuroHPC supercomputer) and ANCHOR-INSTITUTION-HPC (the institution's own HPC facility): this is the federated NREN/national cloud layer, not a supercomputer.
rationale: "national research cloud" / "research cloud" appears only as incidental tokens in the matrix and is not anchored as a sourcing concern; SWITCHengines, EGI Federated Cloud and AARNet are not covered as research-cloud exemplars by any matrix entry (ANCHOR-EUROHPC-SYSTEM covers supercomputers/EGI-federated-cloud-as-HPC-comparator and ANCHOR-INSTITUTION-HPC covers ULHPC). The NREN/national research-cloud sourcing layer with its region-bound exemplars is an uncovered national-infrastructure specificity.
